title: Sort by a member
description:
The range algorithms accept a **projection**: a way of saying which part of each element to compare.

```cpp
std::ranges::sort(players, std::greater{}, &Player::score);   // by score, highest first
```

Using that idea, write:

- `void sortByScore(std::vector<Player>& players)`: highest score first;
- `std::string youngest(const std::vector<Player>& players)`: the name of the player with the smallest age (use `std::ranges::min_element` with a projection). Returns `""` for an empty list.
